456	                # The `combo_name` variable in the code below is not the name of the pushover load combination. Rather it is the name of the primary combination that the pushover load will be added to. Axial loads used to develop Kg are calculated from the displacements stored in `combo_name`.
457	                if log: print('- Calculating geometric stiffness matrix [Kg]')
458	                Kg11, Kg12, Kg21, Kg22 = _partition(model, model.Kg(combo_name, log, sparse, False), D1_indices, D2_indices)
459	                K11 = K11 + Kg11.tocsr()
460	                K12 = K12 + Kg12.tocsr()
461	                # K21 = K21 + Kg21.tocsr()  # This matrix is not used
462	                # K22 = K22 + Kg22.tocsr()  # This matrix is not used
463	
464	        # Dense solver
465	        else:
466	
467	            # Initial stiffness matrix
468	            if log: print('- Calculating elastic stiffness matrix [Ke]')
469	            Ke11, Ke12, Ke21, Ke22 = _partition(model, model.Ke(combo_name, log, check_stability, sparse), D1_indices, D2_indices)
470	
471	            # Calculate the stiffness reduction matrix
472	            if log: print('Calculating plastic reduction matrix [Km]')
473	            Km11, Km12, Km21, Km22 = _partition(model, model.Km(combo_name, push_combo, step_num, log, sparse), D1_indices, D2_indices)
474	
475	            K11 = Ke11 + Km11
476	            K12 = Ke12 + Km12
477	            # K21 = Ke21 + Km21  # This matrix is not used
478	            # K22 = Ke22 + Km22  # This matrix is not used
479	
480	            if P_Delta:
481	                # The `combo_name` variable in the code below is not the name of the pushover load combination. Rather it is the name of the primary combination that the pushover load will be added to. Axial loads used to develop Kg are calculated from the displacements stored in `combo_name`.
482	                if log: print('Calculating geometric stiffness matrix [Kg]')
483	                Kg11, Kg12, Kg21, Kg22 = _partition(model, model.Kg(combo_name, log, sparse, False), D1_indices, D2_indices)
484	                K11 = K11 + Kg11
485	                K12 = K12 + Kg12
486	                # K21 = K21 + Kg21  # This matrix is not used
487	                # K22 = K22 + Kg22  # This matrix is not used
488	
489	        # Calculate the changes to the global displacement vector
490	        if log: print('- Calculating changes to the global displacement vector')
491	        if K11.shape == (0, 0):
492	            # All displacements are known, so D1 is an empty vector
493	            Delta_D1 = []
494	        else:
495	            try:
496	                # Calculate the change in the displacements Delta_D1
497	                if sparse == True:
498	                    # The partitioned stiffness matrix is already in `csr` format. The `@`
499	                    # operator performs matrix multiplication on sparse matrices.
500	                    Delta_D1 = spsolve(K11.tocsr(), subtract(subtract(Delta_P1, Delta_FER1), K12.tocsr() @ D2))
501	                    Delta_D1 = Delta_D1.reshape(len(Delta_D1), 1)
502	                else:
503	                    # The partitioned stiffness matrix is in `csr` format. It will be
504	                    # converted to a 2D dense array for mathematical operations.
505	                    Delta_D1 = solve(K11, subtract(subtract(Delta_P1, Delta_FER1), K12 @ D2))
506	
507	            except:
508	                # Return out of the method if 'K' is singular and provide an error message
509	                raise ValueError('The structure is unstable. Unable to proceed any further with analysis.')
510	
511	        # Tentatively apply the load step so step-validation checks see the current state.
512	        _sum_displacements(model, Delta_D1, D2, D1_indices, D2_indices, model.load_combos[combo_name])
513	
514	        # Assume no need to rerun this load step until one of the validation checks says otherwise.
515	        run_step = False
516	        tc_changed = False
517	        reversal = False
518	        reversal_locations = []
519	
520	        # Check for tension/compression-only status changes caused by this tentative load step.
521	        if _check_TC_convergence(model, combo_name, log, spring_tolerance=tol, member_tolerance=tol) == False:
522	            tc_changed = True
523	            run_step = True
524	
525	        # Unpartition the displacement results from the analysis step for the `lamb` calculations below
526	        Delta_D = _unpartition(model, Delta_D1, D2, D1_indices, D2_indices)
527	        Delta_FER = _unpartition(model, Delta_FER1, Delta_FER2, D1_indices, D2_indices)
528	
529	        # Step through each member in the model and check for plastic load reversal.
530	        for phys_member in model.members.values():
531	
532	            for sub_member in phys_member.sub_members.values():
533	
534	                lamb = sub_member.lamb(Delta_D, combo_name, push_combo, step_num)
535	
536	                # Check for plastic load reversal at the i-node in this load step
537	                if lamb[0, 0] < 0:
538	
539	                    # Flag the load step for reanalysis
540	                    sub_member.i_reversal = True
541	                    reversal = True
542	                    run_step = True
543	                    reversal_locations.append(f'{sub_member.name} i-node')
544	                    if log: print(f'- Plastic load reversal encountered at member {sub_member.name} i-node')
545	
546	                else:
547	
548	                    sub_member.i_reversal = False
549	
550	                # Check for plastic load reversal at the j-node in this load step
551	                if lamb[1, 0] < 0:
552	
553	                    # Flag the load step for reanalysis
554	                    sub_member.j_reversal = True
555	                    reversal = True
556	                    run_step = True
557	                    reversal_locations.append(f'{sub_member.name} j-node')
558	                    if log: print(f'- Plastic load reversal encountered at member {sub_member.name} j-node')
559	
560	                else:
561	
562	                    sub_member.j_reversal = False
563	
564	        # Check if this iteration was valid
565	        if run_step == False:
566	
567	            # Step through each physical member in the model
568	            for phys_member in model.members.values():
569	
570	                # Step through each sub-member of the physical member
571	                for sub_member in phys_member.sub_members.values():
572	
573	                    # Extract the change in the global displacement and fixed end reaction vectors for this member from the full global vectors. The `reshape` method is used to ensure these are column vectors for the matrix operations below.
574	                    Delta_D_member = array([Delta_D[sub_member.i_node.ID*6 + 0, 0],
575	                                            Delta_D[sub_member.i_node.ID*6 + 1, 0],
576	                                            Delta_D[sub_member.i_node.ID*6 + 2, 0],
577	                                            Delta_D[sub_member.i_node.ID*6 + 3, 0],
578	                                            Delta_D[sub_member.i_node.ID*6 + 4, 0],
579	                                            Delta_D[sub_member.i_node.ID*6 + 5, 0],
580	                                            Delta_D[sub_member.j_node.ID*6 + 0, 0],
581	                                            Delta_D[sub_member.j_node.ID*6 + 1, 0],
582	                                            Delta_D[sub_member.j_node.ID*6 + 2, 0],
583	                                            Delta_D[sub_member.j_node.ID*6 + 3, 0],
584	                                            Delta_D[sub_member.j_node.ID*6 + 4, 0],
585	                                            Delta_D[sub_member.j_node.ID*6 + 5, 0]]).reshape(12, 1)
586	                    
587	                    Delta_FER_member = array([Delta_FER[sub_member.i_node.ID*6 + 0, 0],
588	                                              Delta_FER[sub_member.i_node.ID*6 + 1, 0],
589	                                              Delta_FER[sub_member.i_node.ID*6 + 2, 0],
590	                                              Delta_FER[sub_member.i_node.ID*6 + 3, 0],
591	                                              Delta_FER[sub_member.i_node.ID*6 + 4, 0],
592	                                              Delta_FER[sub_member.i_node.ID*6 + 5, 0],
593	                                              Delta_FER[sub_member.j_node.ID*6 + 0, 0],
594	                                              Delta_FER[sub_member.j_node.ID*6 + 1, 0],
595	                                              Delta_FER[sub_member.j_node.ID*6 + 2, 0],
596	                                              Delta_FER[sub_member.j_node.ID*6 + 3, 0],
597	                                              Delta_FER[sub_member.j_node.ID*6 + 4, 0],
598	                                              Delta_FER[sub_member.j_node.ID*6 + 5, 0]]).reshape(12, 1)
599	                    
600	                    # Convert the global displacement and fixed end reaction vectors to local member vectors
601	                    Delta_d = sub_member.T() @ Delta_D_member
602	                    Delta_fer = sub_member.T() @ Delta_FER_member
603	
604	                    # Calculate change in the local end force vector for this load step
605	                    Delta_f = sub_member.f(combo_name, Delta_d, Delta_fer)
606	                    
607	                    sub_member._fxi[combo_name] += Delta_f[0, 0]
608	                    sub_member._fyi[combo_name] += Delta_f[1, 0]
609	                    sub_member._fzi[combo_name] += Delta_f[2, 0]
610	                    sub_member._mxi[combo_name] += Delta_f[3, 0]
611	                    sub_member._myi[combo_name] += Delta_f[4, 0]
612	                    sub_member._mzi[combo_name] += Delta_f[5, 0]
613	                    sub_member._fxj[combo_name] += Delta_f[6, 0]
614	                    sub_member._fyj[combo_name] += Delta_f[7, 0]
615	                    sub_member._fzj[combo_name] += Delta_f[8, 0]
616	                    sub_member._mxj[combo_name] += Delta_f[9, 0]
617	                    sub_member._myj[combo_name] += Delta_f[10, 0]
618	                    sub_member._mzj[combo_name] += Delta_f[11, 0]
619	
620	        else:
621	
622	            tc_changed_last = tc_changed
623	            reversal_locations_last = list(dict.fromkeys(reversal_locations))
624	
625	            # Undo the tentative load step
626	            _sum_displacements(model, -Delta_D1, D2, D1_indices, D2_indices, model.load_combos[combo_name])
627	            if log:
628	                if tc_changed and reversal:
629	                    print('- Restarting load step due to tension/compression-only status change and plastic load reversal')
630	                elif tc_changed:
631	                    print('- Restarting load step due to tension/compression-only status change')
632	                else:
633	                    print('- Restarting load step due to plastic load reversal')

636	def _unpartition(model: FEModel3D, V1: NDArray[float64], V2: NDArray[float64], V1_indices: List[int], V2_indices: List[int]) -> NDArray[float64]:
637	    """Unpartitions a vector and returns it as a global vector including all dofs.
638	
639	    :param model: The finite element model being evaluated
640	    :type model: FEModel3D
641	    :param V1: An array of vector terms corresponding to the unrestrained degrees of freedom.
642	    :type V1: array
643	    :param V2: An array of vector terms corresponding to the degrees of freedom with boundary conditions.
644	    :type V2: array
645	    :param V1_indices: A list of the degree of freedom indices for each term in V1
646	    :type V1_indices: list
647	    :param V2_indices: A list of the degree of freedom indices for each term in V2
648	    :type V2_indices: list
649	    :return: Expanded vector
650	    :rtype: array
651	    """
652	
653	    V = zeros((len(model.nodes)*6, 1))
654	
655	    # Step through each node in the model
656	    for node in model.nodes.values():
657	
658	        # Step through each degree of freedom at the node
659	        for i in range(6):
660	
661	            # Check if the dof is in the list of known vector terms
662	            if node.ID*6 + i in V2_indices:
663	                # Get the vector term for the bounded dof
664	                V[(node.ID*6 + i, 0)] = V2[V2_indices.index(node.ID*6 + i), 0]
665	            else:
666	                # Get the vector term for the unbounded dof
667	                V[(node.ID*6 + i, 0)] = V1[V1_indices.index(node.ID*6 + i), 0]
668	
669	    # Return the vector
670	    return V

673	def _store_displacements(model: FEModel3D, D1: NDArray[float64], D2: NDArray[float64], D1_indices: List[int], D2_indices: List[int], combo: LoadCombo) -> None:
674	    """Stores calculated displacements from the solver into the model's displacement vector `_D` and into each node object in the model
675	
676	    :param model: The finite element model being evaluated.
677	    :type model: FEModel3D
678	    :param D1: An array of calculated displacements
679	    :type D1: array
680	    :param D2: An array of enforced displacements
681	    :type D2: array
682	    :param D1_indices: A list of the degree of freedom indices for each displacement in D1
683	    :type D1_indices: list
684	    :param D2_indices: A list of the degree of freedom indices for each displacement in D2
685	    :type D2_indices: list
686	    :param combo: The load combination to store the displacements for.
687	    :type combo: LoadCombo
688	    """
689	
690	    # The raw results from the solver are partitioned. Unpartition them.
691	    D = _unpartition(model, D1, D2, D1_indices, D2_indices)
692	
693	    if combo != None:
694	
695	        # Store the displacements in the model's global displacement vector
696	        model._D[combo.name] = D
697	
698	        # Store the calculated global nodal displacements into each node object
699	        for node in model.nodes.values():
700	
701	            node.DX[combo.name] = D[node.ID*6 + 0, 0]
702	            node.DY[combo.name] = D[node.ID*6 + 1, 0]
703	            node.DZ[combo.name] = D[node.ID*6 + 2, 0]
704	            node.RX[combo.name] = D[node.ID*6 + 3, 0]
705	            node.RY[combo.name] = D[node.ID*6 + 4, 0]
706	            node.RZ[combo.name] = D[node.ID*6 + 5, 0]

709	def _sum_displacements(model: FEModel3D, Delta_D1: NDArray[float64], Delta_D2: NDArray[float64], D1_indices: List[int], D2_indices: List[int], combo: LoadCombo) -> None:
710	    """Sums calculated displacements for a load step from the solver into the model's displacement vector `_D` and into each node object in the model.
711	
712	    :param model: The finite element model being evaluated.
713	    :type model: FEModel3D
714	    :param Delta_D1: An array of calculated displacements for a load step
715	    :type Delta_D1: array
716	    :param Delta_D2: An array of enforced displacements for a load step
717	    :type Delta_D2: array
718	    :param D1_indices: A list of the degree of freedom indices for each displacement in D1
719	    :type D1_indices: list
720	    :param D2_indices: A list of the degree of freedom indices for each displacement in D2
721	    :type D2_indices: list
722	    :param combo: The load combination to store the displacements for
723	    :type combo: LoadCombo
724	    """
725	
726	    # The raw results from the solver are partitioned. Unpartition them.
727	    Delta_D = _unpartition(model, Delta_D1, Delta_D2, D1_indices, D2_indices)
728	
729	    # Sum the load step's global displacement vector with the model's global displacement vector

730	    model._D[combo.name] += Delta_D
731	
732	    # Sum the load step's calculated global nodal displacements to each node object's global displacement
733	    for node in model.nodes.values():
734	
735	        node.DX[combo.name] += Delta_D[node.ID*6 + 0, 0]
736	        node.DY[combo.name] += Delta_D[node.ID*6 + 1, 0]
737	        node.DZ[combo.name] += Delta_D[node.ID*6 + 2, 0]
738	        node.RX[combo.name] += Delta_D[node.ID*6 + 3, 0]
739	        node.RY[combo.name] += Delta_D[node.ID*6 + 4, 0]
740	        node.RZ[combo.name] += Delta_D[node.ID*6 + 5, 0]

743	def _check_TC_convergence(model: FEModel3D, combo_name: str = "Combo 1", log: bool = True, spring_tolerance: float = 0, member_tolerance: float = 0) -> bool:
744	    """Checks for convergence in tension-only and compression-only analysis.
745	
746	    This function evaluates the status of tension-only and compression-only springs and members
747	    within the finite element model for a given load combination. Its primary purpose is to
748	    determine if the non-linear analysis has converged by checking if any adjustments to the
749	    active status of these elements are required.
750	
751	    The function performs the following checks:
752	    *   **Nodal Spring Convergence**: It iterates through each nodal spring and assesses whether
753	        its active state (whether it is resisting force) aligns with the current displacement
754	        and its tension-only or compression-only designation. If a spring's active
755	        status needs to change based on the displacement and a specified tolerance, the analysis
756	        is flagged as not converged, and the spring's `active` status is updated.
757	    *   **Member Convergence**: It checks each physical member in the model. If a
758	        tension-only member is active but has a maximum axial force greater than the
759	        `member_tolerance` (indicating compression), or if a compression-only member is active
760	        but has a minimum axial force less than `-member_tolerance` (indicating tension),
761	        that physical member and all its sub-members are deactivated. This action
762	        flags the analysis as not converged. A future enhancement is noted to allow elements to
763	        reactivate if deformations indicate they should return to an active state.
764	    *   **Sub-member Reset**: After checking, the `_solved_combo` flag for all sub-members is
765	        reset to `None`. This ensures that they will be resegmented and re-evaluated in subsequent
766	        iterations of the analysis, allowing for further changes as needed for convergence.
767	
768	    :param model: The finite element model currently being evaluated.
769	    :type model: FEModel3D
770	    :param combo_name: The name of the load combination for which the convergence check is
771	        being performed. Defaults to "Combo 1".
772	    :type combo_name: str, optional
773	    :param log: A boolean flag. If `True`, the function prints status updates and information
774	        about the convergence check to the console. Defaults to `True`.
775	    :type log: bool, optional
776	    :param spring_tolerance: A float value representing the displacement tolerance for
777	        tension/compression-only support springs. Springs will switch active state if their
778	        displacement is beyond this tolerance in the disallowed direction. Defaults to 0.
779	    :type spring_tolerance: float, optional
780	    :param member_tolerance: A float value representing the axial force tolerance for
781	        tension/compression-only members. Members will be deactivated if their axial force
782	        is beyond this tolerance in the disallowed direction. Defaults to 0.
783	    :type member_tolerance: float, optional
784	    :return: **True** if all tension-only and compression-only elements have converged (no
785	        changes in active status are needed), **False** otherwise (indicating that further
786	        iterations of the analysis are required).
787	    :rtype: bool
788	    """
789	
790	    # Assume the model has converged until we find out otherwise
791	    convergence = True
792	
793	    # Provide an update to the console if requested by the user
794	    if log:
795	        print("- Checking for tension/compression-only support spring convergence")
796	
797	    # Loop through each node and each directional spring to check and update their active status
798	    for node in model.nodes.values():
799	
800	        for direction in ["DX", "DY", "DZ", "RX", "RY", "RZ"]:
801	            spring = getattr(node, f"spring_{direction}")
802	            displacement = getattr(node, direction)[combo_name]
803	
804	            if spring[1] is not None:
805	                # Determine if the spring should be active based on its designation ('+' or '-') and the displacement
806	                should_be_active = (
807	                    spring[1] == "-" and displacement <= -spring_tolerance
808	                ) or (spring[1] == "+" and displacement >= spring_tolerance)
809	
810	                # Check if there's a need to switch the active state of the spring
811	                if spring[2] != should_be_active:
812	                    spring[2] = should_be_active
813	                    convergence = False
814	
815	    # TODO: Adjust the code below to allow elements to reactivate on subsequent iterations if deformations at element nodes indicate the member goes back into an active state. This will lead to a less conservative and more realistic analysis. Nodal springs (above) already do this.
816	
817	    # Check tension/compression-only springs
818	    if log:
819	        print('- Checking for tension/compression-only spring convergence')
820	
821	    for spring in model.springs.values():
822	
823	        if spring.active[combo_name] == True:
824	
825	            # Check if tension-only conditions exist
826	            if (spring.tension_only == True) and (spring.axial(combo_name) > spring_tolerance):
827	                if log:
828	                    print(f'- Deactivating spring {spring.name}')
829	                spring.active[combo_name] = False
830	                convergence = False
831	
832	            # Check if compression-only conditions exist
833	            elif (spring.comp_only == True) and (spring.axial(combo_name) < -spring_tolerance):
834	                if log:
835	                    print(f'- Deactivating spring {spring.name}')
836	                spring.active[combo_name] = False
837	                convergence = False
838	
839	    # Check tension/compression only members
840	    if log:
841	        print('- Checking for tension/compression-only member convergence')
842	    for phys_member in model.members.values():
843	
844	        # Only run the tension/compression only check if the member is still active
845	        if phys_member.active[combo_name] == True:
846	
847	            # Check if a tension-only conditions exist
848	            if phys_member.tension_only == True and phys_member.max_axial(combo_name) > member_tolerance:
849	
850	                # Deactivate the physical member
851	                if log:
852	                    print(f'- Deactivating member {phys_member.name}')
853	                phys_member.active[combo_name] = False
854	
855	                # Deactivate all the sub-members
856	                for sub_member in phys_member.sub_members.values():
857	                    sub_member.active[combo_name] = False
858	
859	                # Flag the analysis as not converged
860	                convergence = False
861	
862	            # Check if a compression-only conditions exist
863	            elif phys_member.comp_only == True and phys_member.min_axial(combo_name) < - member_tolerance:
864	
865	                # Deactivate the physical member
866	                if log:
867	                    print(f'- Deactivating member {phys_member.name}')
868	                phys_member.active[combo_name] = False
869	
870	                # Deactivate all the sub-members
871	                for sub_member in phys_member.sub_members.values():
872	                    sub_member.active[combo_name] = False
873	
874	                # Flag the analysis as not converged
875	                convergence = False
876	
877	        # Reset the sub-member's flag to unsolved. This will allow it to resolve for the same load combination after subsequent iterations have made further changes.
878	        for sub_member in phys_member.sub_members.values():
879	            sub_member._solved_combo = None
880	
881	    # Return whether the TC analysis has converged
882	    return convergence

885	def _calc_reactions(model: FEModel3D, log: bool = False, combo_tags: List[str] | None = None) -> None:
886	    """
887	    Calculates reactions internally once the model is solved.
888	
889	    Parameters
890	    ----------
891	    model : FEModel3D
892	        The finite element model to calculate reactions for.
893	    log : bool, optional
894	        Prints updates to the console if set to True. Default == False.
895	    combo_tags : string, optional
896	        A list of tags that will be used to identify which load combinations need their reactions calculated. If set to `None` then all load combinations will have their reactions calculated. Default is `None`.
897	    """
898	
899	    # Print a status update to the console
900	    if log:
901	        print('- Calculating reactions')
902	
903	    # Identify which load combinations to evaluate
904	    combo_list = _identify_combos(model, combo_tags)
905	
906	    # Calculate the reactions node by node
907	    for node in model.nodes.values():
908	
909	        # Step through each load combination
910	        for combo in combo_list:
911	
912	            # Initialize reactions for this node and load combination
913	            node.RxnFX[combo.name] = 0.0
914	            node.RxnFY[combo.name] = 0.0
915	            node.RxnFZ[combo.name] = 0.0
916	            node.RxnMX[combo.name] = 0.0
917	            node.RxnMY[combo.name] = 0.0
918	            node.RxnMZ[combo.name] = 0.0
919	
920	            # Determine if the node has any supports
921	            if (node.support_DX or node.support_DY or node.support_DZ
922	            or  node.support_RX or node.support_RY or node.support_RZ):
923	
924	                # Sum the spring end forces at the node
925	                for spring in model.springs.values():
926	
927	                    if spring.i_node == node and spring.active[combo.name] == True:
928	
929	                        # Get the spring's global force matrix
930	                        # Storing it as a local variable eliminates the need to rebuild it every time a term is needed

1142	def _check_statics(model: FEModel3D, combo_tags: List[str] | None = None) -> None:
1143	    '''
1144	    Checks static equilibrium and prints results to the console.
1145	
1146	    Parameters
1147	    ----------
1148	    precision : number
1149	        The number of decimal places to carry the results to.
1150	    '''
1151	
1152	    print('+----------------+')
1153	    print('| Statics Check: |')
1154	    print('+----------------+')
1155	    print('')
1156	
1157	    from prettytable import PrettyTable
1158	
1159	    # Start a blank table and create a header row
1160	    statics_table = PrettyTable()
1161	    statics_table.field_names = ['Load Combination', 'Sum FX', 'Sum RX', 'Sum FY', 'Sum RY', 'Sum FZ', 'Sum RZ', 'Sum MX', 'Sum RMX', 'Sum MY', 'Sum RMY', 'Sum MZ', 'Sum RMZ']
1162	
1163	    # Identify which load combinations to evaluate
1164	    if combo_tags is None:
1165	        combo_list = model.load_combos.values()
1166	    else:
1167	        combo_list = []
1168	        for combo in model.load_combos.values():
1169	            if any(tag in combo.combo_tags for tag in combo_tags):
1170	                combo_list.append(combo)
1171	
1172	    # Step through each load combination
1173	    for combo in combo_list:
1174	
1175	        # Initialize force and moment summations to zero
1176	        SumFX, SumFY, SumFZ = 0.0, 0.0, 0.0
1177	        SumMX, SumMY, SumMZ = 0.0, 0.0, 0.0
1178	        SumRFX, SumRFY, SumRFZ = 0.0, 0.0, 0.0
1179	        SumRMX, SumRMY, SumRMZ = 0.0, 0.0, 0.0
1180	
1181	        # Get the global force vector and the global fixed end reaction vector
1182	        P = model.P(combo.name)
1183	        FER = model.FER(combo.name)
1184	
1185	        # Step through each node and sum its forces
1186	        for node in model.nodes.values():
1187	
1188	            # Get the node's coordinates
1189	            X = node.X
1190	            Y = node.Y
1191	            Z = node.Z
1192	
1193	            # Get the nodal forces
1194	            FX = P[node.ID*6+0][0] - FER[node.ID*6+0][0]
1195	            FY = P[node.ID*6+1][0] - FER[node.ID*6+1][0]
1196	            FZ = P[node.ID*6+2][0] - FER[node.ID*6+2][0]
1197	            MX = P[node.ID*6+3][0] - FER[node.ID*6+3][0]
1198	            MY = P[node.ID*6+4][0] - FER[node.ID*6+4][0]
1199	            MZ = P[node.ID*6+5][0] - FER[node.ID*6+5][0]
1200	
1201	            # Get the nodal reactions
1202	            RFX = node.RxnFX[combo.name]
1203	            RFY = node.RxnFY[combo.name]
1204	            RFZ = node.RxnFZ[combo.name]
1205	            RMX = node.RxnMX[combo.name]
1206	            RMY = node.RxnMY[combo.name]
1207	            RMZ = node.RxnMZ[combo.name]
1208	
1209	            # Sum the global forces
1210	            SumFX += FX
1211	            SumFY += FY
1212	            SumFZ += FZ
1213	            SumMX += MX - FY*Z + FZ*Y
1214	            SumMY += MY + FX*Z - FZ*X
1215	            SumMZ += MZ - FX*Y + FY*X
1216	
1217	            # Sum the global reactions
1218	            SumRFX += RFX
1219	            SumRFY += RFY
1220	            SumRFZ += RFZ
1221	            SumRMX += RMX - RFY*Z + RFZ*Y
1222	            SumRMY += RMY + RFX*Z - RFZ*X
1223	            SumRMZ += RMZ - RFX*Y + RFY*X
1224	
1225	        # Add the results to the table
1226	        statics_table.add_row([combo.name, '{:.3g}'.format(SumFX), '{:.3g}'.format(SumRFX),
1227	                                            '{:.3g}'.format(SumFY), '{:.3g}'.format(SumRFY),
1228	                                            '{:.3g}'.format(SumFZ), '{:.3g}'.format(SumRFZ),
1229	                                            '{:.3g}'.format(SumMX), '{:.3g}'.format(SumRMX),
1230	                                            '{:.3g}'.format(SumMY), '{:.3g}'.format(SumRMY),
1231	                                            '{:.3g}'.format(SumMZ), '{:.3g}'.format(SumRMZ)])
1232	
1233	    # Print the static check table
1234	    print(statics_table)
1235	    print('')

def _solve_stiffness(K11, RHS: NDArray[float64], sparse: bool) -> NDArray[float64]:
    """Solves the partitioned stiffness system `K11 @ D1 = RHS` for the unknown displacements.

    A stiffness matrix that has been partitioned down to the structure's unrestrained degrees of freedom is singular whenever the structure can undergo rigid body motion (an instability or mechanism). Factorization-based solvers only fail on exactly-zero pivots, while the stiffness matrix of an unstable structure is typically singular only to within floating-point resolution, so the solver can otherwise return enormous, physically meaningless displacements that differ between the sparse and dense solvers. To keep both solver modes consistent, this helper verifies that the partitioned stiffness matrix is numerically non-singular before results are returned, and raises `numpy.linalg.LinAlgError` when it is not. The threshold used in either mode is the standard round-off-level rank tolerance, so a well-posed (stable) model is never flagged.

    :param K11: The partitioned stiffness matrix for the unknown displacements.
    :type K11: ndarray or scipy sparse matrix
    :param RHS: The partitioned right-hand-side vector (applied loads minus fixed end reactions and effects of known displacements).
    :type RHS: numpy array
    :param sparse: Indicates whether `K11` is held in a sparse storage format.
    :type sparse: bool
    :raises numpy.linalg.LinAlgError: Occurs when the stiffness matrix is numerically singular, which indicates an unstable structure.
    :return: The calculated displacements `D1` as an n x 1 array.
    :rtype: numpy array
    """

    # Round-off-level rank tolerance, e.g. the tolerance `numpy.linalg.matrix_rank` uses
    rank_tol = max(K11.shape)*np.finfo(np.float64).eps

    if sparse == True:

        # Import the sparse direct solver
        from scipy.sparse.linalg import splu

        # Factor the stiffness matrix. SuperLU raises a `RuntimeError` if the matrix is exactly singular.
        lu = splu(K11.tocsc())

        # Guard against numerical (inexact) singularity, which SuperLU's exact check cannot catch. A factorization pivot at round-off level relative to the largest pivot indicates the matrix is rank deficient to working precision.
        pivots = np.abs(lu.U.diagonal())
        if pivots.size == 0 or pivots.max() == 0.0 or pivots.min() <= pivots.max()*rank_tol:
            raise LinAlgError('The stiffness matrix is numerically singular to within floating-point precision.')

Done. The workbench now reports a controlled case failure for the unstable frame and unchanged finite results for the control — consistently across both matrix-storage modes.

## Diagnosis

Case_a's entered topology has only **5 restraints in 3-D** (6 are required: pin at `p` + DY/DZ at `q`), so the frame is a mechanism — its stiffness matrix is singular, but only to floating-point resolution (σmin/σmax ≈ 5e-18). The snapshot's solve path only caught *exactly* singular matrices (LAPACK `LinAlgError` / SuperLU's exact-zero-pivot check), so both solvers silently returned enormous garbage that differed by mode (2.86e8 vs 6.3e7) — a misleading "solution" for an unstable structure, contrary to the documented contract that both storage modes "provide the same structural solution". Everything else verified healthy: beam theory exact (PL³/3EI, PL³/48EI), sparse/dense assembly bit-identical, reactions and `check_statics`/`check_stability` behaved per docs.

## Fix

- Added `Analysis._solve_stiffness()` (`source/Pynite/Analysis.py:170`): solves the partitioned system but first guards numerical singularity at round-off level (rank tolerance `n·eps`):
  - sparse — `splu` factorization (reused for the solve); raises if any factorization pivot is at round-off level relative to the largest pivot; exact singularity raises via SuperLU,
  - dense — smallest-singular-value check, then the usual `solve`,
  - non-finite results also raise.
  It raises `LinAlgError`, which each call site converts to its documented exception (the "stiffness matrix is singular... rigid body motion" error for `analyze`/`analyze_linear`; the documented `ValueError`s in P-Delta and pushover).
- Routed the four linear solve sites through it: `Analysis._first_order` (used by `analyze` and pushover preload), `Analysis._PDelta`, `Analysis._pushover_step`, and `FEModel3D.analyze_linear`.

## Verification

- `reproduce.py` (run repeatedly): case_a → `Exception` in **both** modes; control → finite, reaction 6.25 (exact propped-cantilever 5wL/8) in both modes.
- Stable analyses unchanged and mode-consistent: cantilever/SS-beam match theory to 15 digits, 3-D skew member identical results, P-Delta amplification consistent, enforced-displacement path exact, tension-only brace converges identically, `num_steps` 1 vs 4 identical, multi-load-combo results identical.
- Documented checks preserved: `check_stability` still reports/aborts on nodal instabilities pre-solution; `check_statics` prints the balance table with applied/reaction pairs canceling.
- A randomized 25-model battery confirmed sparse==dense (or identical failure class) plus force/moment equilibrium about the origin; a stabilized variant of case_a yields finite, consistent, equilibrium-exact results.
